Right now, we are looking for personable Production Team Lead to assist the Bakery Production Manager to share their love of fresh bread with our loyal customers.

 Lead and work as part of a small team to bake products from scratch early each morning, following carefully crafted recipes

 This posting is for an existing vacancy 
 Internal applicants should apply with your work e-mail address . External applicants are considered only after the internal posting process has been completed. Only applicants chosen for an interview will be contacted. 
 SUMMARY OF DUTIES 
 Reporting to the Supervisor Monitoring & Enforcement Operations.  Inspects and enforces City By-laws on pollution control and abatement.  Performs sewer and water investigations to ensure compliance with Provincial Legislation and City By-laws. 
 GENERAL DUTIES 
 Inspects and reports on premises such as industrial, commercial and institutional facilities to ensure compliance with Municipal regulations.  Advises facility operator on non-compliance issues while maintaining and delivering a customer focused service. 
 Assesses requests for Sewer Discharge Permits by reviewing engineering reports, schematics, conducting on-site inspections and analysing background water quality data with requestor. 
 Participates in the implementation and maintenance of an industrial sampling program to ensure users are in compliance with current legislation. 
 Investigates non-compliance with sewer use by-law.  Initiates appropriate action. 
 Collects samples of industrial effluents, sewer outfalls, spilled materials, etc, that may or may not be used as evidence in a court of law, reviews and interprets laboratory reports, implements courses of action to be taken to mitigate harm to City infrastructure or environmental degradation. 
 Reviews plans, inspects and assesses pollution control practices to ensure compliance with legislation. 
 Implements and monitors traffic control plans and follows various other Health and Safety practices as per current legislation. 
 Operates equipment such as sewer samplers, gas detectors, pH probes, flow meters, 2-way radios, cell phones, , laptop computers, GPS devices, and other various tools. 
 Prepares and follows up on notices of violation, issues tickets, lays charges and orders, delivers summonses, prepares and gives evidence in court. 
 Facilitates compliance meetings and documents corrective actions. 
 Promotes a service oriented culture and focus within the section. 
 Receives and answers inquiries of a technical nature from public, staff, other departments, consultants, municipal and government agencies related to major responsibilities. 
 Writes reports, composes correspondence related to major responsibilities. 
 Develops and assists in developing policies and procedures related to major responsibilities. 
 Ability to deal effectively with elected officials, representatives of other levels of government, management, peers, staff and the general public. 
 Thorough knowledge and understanding of statutes, regulations and by-laws affecting the department/section. 
 Represents the division before public meetings, industry representatives and other government officials. 
 Provides orientation for new staff, trains and develops new staff. 
 Works in accordance with the provisions of applicable Health and Safety legislation and all City of Hamilton corporate and departmental policies and procedures related to Occupational Health and Safety 
 Performs other duties as assigned which are directly related to the major responsibilities of the job. 
 QUALIFICATIONS 
 Demonstrated knowledge of chemical and environmental engineering theories and principles, normally acquired by attaining a diploma from a two-year Community College course in an accredited Engineering Technician program in Chemical or Environmental studies or related field or the equivalent combination of relevant education and work experience. 
 Demonstrated experience and knowledge in sewer sampling, pre-treatment systems, spill responses related to duties listed above. 
 Thorough knowledge and understanding of methods, statutes, regulations and by-laws affecting the department/section, including Health and Safety and Environmental Regulations applied to environmental sampling and spills. 
 Demonstrated ability to investigate infractions and to make sound decisions whether to issue courtesy warnings or notices where by-laws have been breached. 
 Must be available for stand-by rotation program to respond to emergency situations such as chemical spills. 
 Ability to act independently, with strong problem solving and decision-making skills. 
 Demonstrated ability to conduct investigations, including root cause analysis, evidence collection and proper documentation and note taking. 
 Demonstrated ability to prepare written reports, briefs, evidence and practice document control by entering/maintaining information in databases, electronic files and tracking sheets. 
 Excellent people skills with an emphasis on customer service. 
 Must have excellent verbal and written communication, initiative and organizational skills. 
 Highly effective negotiation, presentation and interpersonal skills. 
 Demonstrated ability to perform as a member of a team. 
 Experience in a computerized environment with working knowledge of Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, GIS and database software. 
 Demonstrated ability to interpret laboratory results and engineering schematics. 
 Possesses a demonstrated record of customer focus, public relations, innovation/creativity, team participation, and is committed to results. 
 Possesses a high level of personal integrity and communication ability. 
 Must possess a valid Class "G" Driver's Licence and the provision of a car by the individual for use on the job, and proof thereof is required after hire. 
 Demonstrated knowledge of pre-treatment systems; wastewater treatment processes; industrial processes; and pollution prevention practices. 
 This position requires the ability to lift loads of up to 50 pounds on a daily basis.

 Choosing BDC as your employer means working in a healthy, inclusive, and skilled workplace that puts forward the best conditions to bring together unique teams where employees are empowered to act. It also means being at the centre of ambitious economic and financial projects to see further and to do things differently, to fuel the success of Canadian entrepreneurs.
 Choosing BDC as your employer also means: 
 Flexible and competitive benefits , including an Employee Savings and Investment Plan where BDC matches part of your voluntary contributions, a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, a $750 wellness and health care spending account, to name a few   
 In addition to paid vacation each year, five personal days , sick days as necessary , and our offices are closed from December 25 to January 1 
 A hybrid work model that truly balances work and personal life
 Opportunities for learning , training and development , and much more... 
 Explore the BDC Way in our Culture Book 
 POSITION OVERVIEW 
 The Associate is an integral member of the BDC Capital Fund Investments team and is involved in all aspects of the investment and portfolio management process. You will help the team build and manage a diversified portfolio of fund investments.
 Your primary focus will be BDC Capital's pre-seed and seed fund investment activities. You will support the sourcing, evaluation, execution and management of investments in venture capital funds that invest at the earliest stages of company formation. You will also contribute to the development of BDC Capital's relationships with emerging managers and key participants in Canada's startup and innovation ecosystem. 
 CHALLENGES TO BE MET 
 Sourcing: Screen and assess a high volume of emerging fund managers to identify the most promising opportunities. Collaborate in the preparation of regular market reviews and prioritization analyses.
 Investing: Collaborate in the evaluation and assessment of fund investment opportunities; conducting initial and detailed reviews of investment opportunities; communicating with fund managers and references; preparing investment memorandums and recommendations; and supporting the negotiation of terms and conditions.
 Portfolio management: Collaborate with the Directors in the management of portfolio fund investments, including monitoring underlying portfolio company investments, fund performance and other related activities; communicating with fund managers; attending LPACs and AGMs; preparing analysis; and preparing presentations for senior management. 
 Fund operations: Collaborate in the management of portfolio monitoring and financial systems, including the oversight of the data collection process; the review of quarterly and annual reporting; and the periodic review of systems and processes.
 Ecosystem development: Keep abreast of industry activity and best practices and contribute to positive industry visibility by establishing and maintaining continuous interaction with key industry players and attending investment conferences and other relevant events.
 Fund strategy: Conduct research, market analysis, portfolio review, performance analysis and benchmarking. This involves gathering market data; analyzing research reports; interviewing fund managers and industry experts; and building fund financial models. This includes monitoring developments in the pre-seed and seed venture capital market in Canada and internationally. 
 Team meetings: Participate in team discussions, including pipeline management; review of investment opportunities and investment recommendations; and fund investment strategy. 
 Pre-Seed and Seed Specialization 
 Prior experience evaluating pre-seed and seed-stage venture funds is an asset, not a prerequisite. We are looking for a person with the curiosity, analytical capabilities and investment judgment to develop a strong understanding of emerging managers, manager differentiation and the dynamics shaping early-stage venture capital markets.
 The successful candidate will build knowledge of the Canadian and global venture capital ecosystem, including the factors that contribute to successful fund formation, manager development and long-term investment performance.
 WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR 
 Bachelor's degree in Commerce or equivalent (concentration in finance or accounting is preferred);
 CFA (completed or in progress) and/or Master's degree in Finance or a related field would be an asset;
 Three or more years of relevant work experience; experience in venture capital, private equity, fund investments or other areas of the innovation ecosystem would be an asset;
 Strong research, financial modeling and analytical skills;
 Strong attention to detail;
 Demonstrated initiative and curiosity to look beyond surface facts and conduct comprehensive, fact-based, value-added research;
 Interest in venture capital, emerging fund managers and the dynamics of pre-seed and seed-stage investing;
 Ability to assess information from multiple sources and develop well-supported insights regarding investment opportunities, market trends and manager differentiation;
 Ability to articulate and present facts and ideas effectively both verbally and in writing;
 Excellent organizational skills with the ability to prioritize, manage multiple tasks, and work independently using initiative and good judgment to assess priorities;
 Exercise discretion and professionalism in handling sensitive situations and maintaining an appropriate level of confidentiality;
 Excellent interpersonal as well as written and oral communication skills in English; French fluency would be a strong asset.
 Proficiency with AI tools

 Faire is a technology wholesale platform built on the belief that the future is local. At Faire, we're using the power of tech, data, and machine learning to connect this thriving community of entrepreneurs across the globe. Picture your favorite boutique in town — we help them discover the best products from around the world to sell in their stores.  The Discovery Search team (Search FX) sits at the intersection of search, evaluation, and personalization shaping how retailers find the products they love. Our mission is to build the most intuitive, intelligent, and delightful discovery experience in wholesale: one that feels less like a search engine and more like a trusted merchant with an encyclopedic knowledge of what's in stock and what will sell.
 As a Staff Engineer on the Search FX team, you will be a primary technical architect for our retailer-facing search surfaces. You will own the technical roadmap for search, recommendations, and Gen-AI experiences that drive a meaningful share of marketplace engagement. You will bridge the gap between high-scale infrastructure and world-class UX, helping unify retrieval, ranking, and personalization into a cohesive, high-performance system.
 You’re excited about this role because... 
 You will own the technical vision: Define the end-to-end architecture for Faire's search and discovery experience, ensuring it is fast, relevant, and deeply personalized.
 You’ll build at the AI frontier: Integrate LLM-powered capabilities, such as natural language search and intelligent query understanding, directly into the product.
 You’ll solve complex scale problems: Help build high-scale, low-latency systems that navigate millions of products while meeting strict industry latency benchmarks.
 You’ll drive cross-functional impact: Partner closely with Data Science, Product, and Design to iterate on ranking models and UX components.
 You’ll be a mentor and leader: Foster a culture of engineering excellence and ownership, upskilling the team on technical expertise and decision-making.

 Architect Next-Gen Search: Lead the design of composable grids, intent-aware routing, and orchestration layers that unify retrieval and ranking.
 Modernize Query Understanding: Leverage LLMs to consolidate the QU stack, improving accuracy for long-tail queries and edge cases.
 Optimize Performance: Drive initiatives to increase retrieval candidates (e.g., 10x growth) while maintaining stable search latency.
 Launch AI-Driven Features: Develop systems like "Search Missions" that use offline pipelines and LLMs to recover failed search sessions through expanded queries.
 Bridge AI and UX: Work with client engineers on SDUI and React Server Components to improve performance and developer velocity for dynamic search layouts.
 System Ownership: Take accountability for the reliability and observability of the search funnel, from query planner refactors to real-time retrieval monitoring.

 Domain Expertise: knowledge of search/query processing, including traditional, semantic, and hybrid frameworks (e.g., Elasticsearch, Lucene).

 Strategic Leadership: Demonstrated ability to contribute to team strategy without supervision and influence the broader organizational roadmap.

Put your accounting expertise to work. Help shape what comes next. 
 At Acuity Insights, we’re strengthening our accounting operations, improving our systems, and finding better ways to work. We’re looking for an experienced accountant who can take on complex work independently and help us build a stronger, more effective accounting function.
 As our Senior Accountant, you’ll own significant areas of the accounting cycle, from close and financial reporting to revenue, reconciliations, and audit readiness. You’ll also help strengthen the accuracy and reliability of our financial and business reporting, including recurring revenue metrics, while contributing accounting insights to budgeting, forecasting, and financial analysis.
 You’ll work closely with our Controller and alongside a small accounting team, bringing the judgment to work through complex accounting questions, identify root causes, and see issues through to resolution. Your experience will also help strengthen the team through shared knowledge, guidance, and better ways of working.
 There’s plenty to improve and build. We’re preparing for a new accounting system, exploring automation and AI, and reducing the manual work that slows us down. You’ll have the opportunity to lead meaningful improvements while helping make our accounting processes more reliable and scalable.
 If you enjoy solving complex accounting problems, sharing what you know, and finding better ways to get things done, there’s a lot here for you to contribute.
 Before you apply: This is a fully remote role open to candidates anywhere in Canada. We’re hiring for an existing, open position. You’re welcome to use AI thoughtfully when preparing your application and conversations with our team. Just make sure what you share reflects your own experience, thinking, and judgment. During live conversations, please don’t use AI to generate responses unless invited to do so. 
 The Work You’ll Do
 In your first few weeks, you’ll get to know Acuity’s business, current accounting systems, processes, and controls, working alongside our Controller and accounting team to understand how things work today and where we can improve.
 We’re working toward a five-business-day close, and you’ll play an important role in helping us get there.
 Own complex accounting work 
 You’ll own significant areas of the accounting cycle, including complex journal entries and reconciliations, month-end and year-end close, financial reporting, and audit support. You’ll also review reconciliations and supporting schedules prepared by the team, investigate unusual items, and ensure the close is complete and ready for Controller review.
 When accounting questions are complex or something doesn’t reconcile, you’ll dig into the details, investigate root causes, and use sound judgment to recommend the right path forward. Your work will help us build a faster, more reliable close supported by strong processes and controls.
 Strengthen revenue accounting and reporting 
 You’ll provide senior-level review and oversight of revenue accounting, including revenue recognition, deferred revenue, reconciliations, and related reporting. Working with teammates responsible for invoicing, receivables, and recurring revenue schedules, you’ll connect business activity with accounting records.
 You’ll review accounting outputs, investigate discrepancies, and resolve complex or unusual transactions. You’ll help ensure revenue is recognized appropriately, supporting schedules reconcile to the general ledger, and financial and business reporting is accurate and reliable..
 Turn accounting information into reliable financial insight 
 You’ll help ensure the accounting information behind our financial and business reporting is accurate, consistent, and reliable, including the preparation and reconciliation of recurring revenue metrics.
 You’ll contribute accounting insights and historical context to financial analysis, budgeting, and forecasting, helping the business make informed decisions. You’ll also support cash management through short-term cash forecasting, cash flow variance analysis, and visibility into upcoming cash requirements.
 Help modernize our accounting systems 
 We’re preparing to move to a new accounting platform. You’ll contribute your accounting expertise to the transition, from defining requirements and improving workflows to data validation, testing, and migration.
 You’ll also have opportunities to take ownership of meaningful improvements that make our systems and processes more efficient, reliable, and easier to use.
 Improve how Accounting works 
 You’ll look beyond your own responsibilities to identify recurring problems, unnecessary manual work, and opportunities to simplify processes, strengthen controls, and use automation or AI thoughtfully.
 You’ll help turn those opportunities into practical improvements, while strengthening documentation, sharing knowledge, and building better coverage across the team.
 The goal is an accounting function that spends less time moving information around and more time on the work where expertise and judgment matter.
 Who You’ll Work With and How
 You’ll report to our Controller and work alongside a small team of accountants. You’ll have meaningful ownership of your work while sharing knowledge, solving problems together, and helping strengthen how Accounting operates.
 Accounting connects to almost every part of Acuity, so you’ll work closely with people across the business:
 Your Accounting teammates , to work through complex questions, share expertise, strengthen coverage, and improve how the team works.
 Revenue Operations , to connect contracts, billing, revenue, and the information that supports accurate financial reporting.
 People & Culture , on payroll, employee-related accounting, and the processes that connect our teams.
 Leaders and budget owners , to understand the context behind transactions, resolve accounting questions, and support reliable financial information.
 External partners , including auditors and other Finance partners, to support reporting, compliance, and audit readiness.
 You’ll work with a high degree of independence, but not in isolation. You’ll know when to make decisions, when to bring others in, and how to build trust through clear communication, sound judgment, and reliable follow-through.
 What Success Looks Like
 In your first three months, you’ll build an understanding of Acuity’s business, accounting cycle, systems, and controls. You’ll begin taking ownership of key accounting responsibilities, building relationships across the business, and identifying opportunities to improve how work gets done.
 By six months, you’ll independently own significant areas of the accounting cycle, confidently work through complex reconciliations and accounting questions, and identify issues before they become problems. You’ll also begin turning improvement opportunities into practical changes.
 By the end of your first year, you’ll be a trusted source of accounting expertise, handling complex work with minimal guidance and contributing improvements beyond your own responsibilities. Your impact will be visible in stronger processes, better controls, and greater shared knowledge and coverage across Accounting.
 How You’ll Succeed
 You’ll likely thrive here if you:
 Take ownership. You follow work through to resolution, surface issues early, and take responsibility for accurate, reliable outcomes.
 Look beyond the numbers. You investigate discrepancies, ask questions, and connect the dots to understand what’s really happening.
 Balance judgment with momentum. You respect accounting standards and controls while knowing when to make decisions, move forward, or bring others in.
 Look for better ways of working. Y ou notice unnecessary complexity and manual effort, finding practical opportunities to improve processes, systems, and controls.
 Share what you know. You document your work, offer guidance, and help build stronger knowledge and coverage across Accounting.
 Use technology thoughtfully. You explore how systems, automation, and AI can improve your work, applying the same judgment and care you’d bring to any accounting decision.
 Are comfortable building while doing. You work effectively as processes evolve, bringing structure to your own work while helping strengthen how Accounting operates.
 As the Finance function evolves, you’ll have opportunities to deepen your expertise, take on broader ownership, and contribute to larger systems and process improvements.
 Experience That Will Help You Hit the Ground Running
 You’ll bring strong technical accounting expertise, sound judgment, and the ability to independently own complex work. Your experience will include:
 Independently owning significant areas of month-end and year-end close, including journal entries, balance sheet reconciliations, working papers, and general ledger accounting.
 Preparing or supporting financial reporting, ensuring the underlying accounting records are accurate, complete, and well supported.
 Working across revenue recognition, invoicing, receivables, or other core accounting activities, with an understanding of how they connect through the accounting cycle.
 Investigating complex accounting questions and discrepancies, applying accounting principles and professional judgment to determine the right path forward.
 Supporting external audits and maintaining strong documentation, controls, and audit readiness.
 Improving accounting processes, workflows, or systems to reduce manual work, strengthen reliability, and make the work more efficient.
 Working independently in evolving environments, knowing when to make decisions, collaborate, or escalate.
 Additional experience that would be valuable: Recurring revenue reporting, deferred revenue, budgeting, forecasting, cash management, or accounting system implementations.
 Our current Finance systems include Xero, Dext, Airwallex, Plooto, and Stripe. You don’t need experience with these specific tools, but you should be comfortable working with cloud-based accounting systems and learning new technology.
 A CPA designation, or progress toward one, is an asset but not required. Equivalent expertise developed through experience is equally valued.
 How We Support You
 Transparent compensation. A salary between $95,000 - $105,000 CAD, aligned to role scope, experience, and internal equity.
 Learning that grows with you. A $3,000 annual learning budget to invest in your development, whether that’s deepening your accounting expertise, building new technical skills, or exploring new areas of interest.
 Shared success. Access to employee stock options, so you share in the value you help create.
 Remote-first work. Fully remote within Canada, with up to six weeks per year to work internationally.
 Time to rest and reset. Self-directed vacation (most teammates take 4–6 weeks annually), monthly Acuity Days (a collective Friday off), plus a two-week company-wide closure each December.
 Comprehensive care. Health benefits from day one for you and your dependents.
 Future-focused support. A 2% GRSP matching program to help you plan ahead.
 Support for growing families. A 16-week parental leave top-up beyond EI, available to all parents.
 What Happens After You Apply
 We review every application carefully. Whether you apply directly, are referred, or connect through a recruiter or hiring manager, you’ll receive equal consideration.
 We don’t use AI to evaluate applications, though you may be automatically screened out if you don’t meet baseline requirements (e.g. Canadian residency and valid work authorization). In some interviews, AI may help with note-taking, but all evaluations and decisions are made by real humans.
 Our interviews are two-way conversations. We want to understand your career, abilities, and goals, and help you assess whether this opportunity and team are the right fit for you. 
 Steps in the Process 
 Our hiring process typically takes 2–4 weeks from initial conversation to final decision. 
 Application Review. A real person reviews your application for potential fit.
 Intro Conversation. A conversation with a member of our Talent team to learn about your career journey, what you’re looking for next, and to introduce you to Acuity, Casper, and the role.
 Conversation with the Manager. You’ll meet our Controller to explore the accounting work you’ve owned, how you approach complex problems, and the decisions you’ve made along the way. If you have an example of real work you’re proud of and can share, bring it along. It could be a process you’ve improved or a way you’ve used technology, automation, or AI to work more effectively. No need to prepare anything new or formal. It’s an opportunity to share how you approached the work, the judgment you applied, and what you learned.
 Team Conversations. You’ll meet a few of the people you’d work with closely to explore how you collaborate, solve problems, and improve ways of working, while getting a better feel for what working together would be like.
 Decision. The hiring manager reviews feedback from the interview team and typically makes a decision within 2 to 4 business days.
 Offer & Reference Checks. If it’s a match, we’ll move to references and a formal offer.
 Life at Acuity Insights
 We’re a remote-first team of 135+ people, built around trust, flexibility, and giving people meaningful ownership of their work.
 Remote-first doesn’t mean working in isolation. We collaborate closely across teams, communicate thoughtfully across time zones, and create intentional opportunities to connect, while protecting the flexibility and focus that make remote work valuable.
 Day to day, you can expect:
 High trust and autonomy in how you get your work done.
 Thoughtful, async-friendly communication across a distributed team.
 Opportunities to share ideas and perspectives that help inform our direction.
 Colleagues who are generous with their expertise, challenge thinking, and learn from one another.
 A culture of curiosity, continuous learning, and thoughtful experimentation, including how we use AI.
 A sustainable approach to work that values impact over performative busyness.
 As we grow, we’re deliberate about evolving how we work without adding process for process’s sake. We want people to have the clarity, context, relationships, and room to make good decisions, challenge assumptions, and contribute to work that matters.
 About Acuity Insights
 At Acuity Insights, we build research-backed technology that helps higher education institutions better understand people, make informed decisions, and support learner development.
 We believe people are more than their grades, and that human potential can be understood, nurtured, and developed throughout the educational journey.
 Our products support institutions and learners at different stages, from identifying potential and making fairer admissions decisions to supporting education, professional development, and growth. Our Casper situational judgment test, developed by researchers at McMaster University, has been completed by over 1 million applicants and is backed by nearly 20 years of research.
 Today, we’re building toward a more connected ecosystem that brings together assessment, education, and development. By combining research, technology, and responsible AI, we aim to help institutions make better decisions, create more meaningful learning experiences, and support people in reaching their potential.
 We’re at a point in our evolution where the work we do today is helping shape what’s possible tomorrow. And the people who join us will have an opportunity to contribute to that future.

 JOB SUMMARY 
 The Project Engineer is at the forefront of high-impact, multidisciplinary engineering projects that contribute directly to the corporate priorities that drive our company forward. Key responsibilities include implementing the capital program through the project management of major substation builds and renewals, critical grid modernization initiatives, and more. DO YOU BELIEVE IN THE POWER OF COMMUNITY?


Then Jobber might be the place for you! We’re looking for a Senior Brand Partnerships Manager to be part of our  Brand Marketing and Communications team in our Marketing department.

Jobber exists to help people in small businesses be successful. We work with small home service businesses, like your local plumbers, painters, and landscapers, to transform the way service is delivered through technology. With Jobber they can quote, schedule, invoice, and collect payments from their customers, while providing an easy and professional customer experience. Running a small business today isn’t like it used to be—the way we consume and deliver service is changing rapidly, technology is evolving, and customers expect more. That’s why we put the power and flexibility in their hands to run their businesses how, where, and when they want!

Our culture of transparency, inclusivity, collaboration, and innovation has been recognized by Great Place to Work, Canada’s Most Admired Corporate Cultures, and more. Jobber has also been named on the Globe and Mail’s Canada’s Top Growing Companies list, and Deloitte Canada’s Technology Fast 50™, Enterprise Fast 15, and Technology Fast 500™ lists. With an Executive team that has over thirty years of industry experience of leading the way, we’ve come a long way from our first customer in 2011—but we’ve just scratched the surface of what we want to accomplish for our customers https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EkfZmHrRLx4&list=PLoktA_D-2UEnxMLfCe93bANKXVXd2bdN8&index=23.

The team:

When it comes to telling the world about Jobber and moving new people through a funnel, Marketing is your team. They handle everything from spreading awareness, to answering “What's Jobber?,” to getting new customers in the door, to turning those customers into Jobber advocates!

Jobber's Brand Marketing and Communications team works on programs and campaigns that grow awareness of Jobber, including our annual Jobber Summit event, our Jobber Grants program, and many other online and offline experiences we collaborate on with our community to pull off! The following areas fall under Brand Marketing and Communications: Brand Partnerships, Communications, Community Programs, Events, Public Relations, and Social Media. Our Marketing department is very collaborative, so you'll have the support of your colleagues from Product Marketing to the Jobber Creative Studio to make the magic happen.

The role:

Our Brand Partnerships team manages both short term and long term relationships with online influencers to build awareness of Jobber and recommend Jobber software to their communities, ultimately driving new Jobber customers. It's one of our acquisition channels and we're building it into a best-in-class program.

Reporting to the Senior Manager of Brand Partnerships, the Senior Brand Partnerships Manager is a senior individual contributor role for someone who wants to shape where this channel goes next. Half of your time goes to your own roster of brand partners and the spend behind it, recruiting, coaching, negotiating, and hitting a monthly number. The other half is bigger: you'll build the strategy for how we help our strongest partners grow further, across the entire program, forecast what it's worth, prove it on your own roster, and roll it out to the team.

The ideal candidate has done this before. You've looked across a whole roster and seen where the real headroom was, not just where the gaps were. You've built a strategy, set a number against it, and been held to it. You're comfortable in the data, confident in a negotiation, and good at getting people who don't report to you to change how they work. You have a point of view about where creator marketing is heading and the operating discipline to prove it.

The Senior Brand Partnerships Manager will:

 - Own a roster. You'll recruit, coach, and grow your own roster of brand partners and the spend behind it—full cycle, from first conversation and negotiation through onboarding, ongoing coaching, and renewal.

 - Help great partners 2x their results. With visibility across our whole partner network, you'll work out what our most successful partners do differently, and turn that into something every partner can benefit from. The best partners in this program are still nowhere near their ceiling, and finding what takes them there is the heart of this role.

 - Build the strategy for partner growth. You'll develop the strategy, set the targets and forecast, design what we try, and test across the team. This is work that doesn't exist yet—you'll create it.

 - Implement growth strategies. Working collaboratively across our team, you’ll implement and launch strategies to grow our performing talent into top performers. You’ll set targets, work with other reps to activate their partners, and report on performance regularly to prove what’s working to drive incremental sales.

 - Turn it into plays the team can run. Every improvement you create should become something repeatable. You'll document it, train the team on it, and make sure it sticks, then be honest about what isn't working and change course.

 - Dig deep into the data. You'll analyze channel performance, report on results, and translate what you find into action.

 - Negotiate with judgment. You'll handle complex partnership negotiations and contracts, using strong judgment on brand fit and brand risk, and collaborating with our Public Relations and Legal teams where a partnership carries exposure.

 - Be a brand champion. You'll protect and grow the reach and reputation of our brand through the partners we work with, and contribute ideas for campaigns, events, and resources that make our program one people want to be part of.

 - Raise the level of the team. You'll share insights and learnings, coach and support other Brand Partnership reps, and help set the standard for what great looks like here.



To be successful, you’ll need:

 - Extensive marketing and influencer partnership experience. You’ll have a track record of measurable, social-driven results that contribute to new business (sales) and revenue.

 - A track record of making good performance great. You've taken programs or partners that were already working and found meaningful additional growth in them, helping them reach a level they hadn’t before, and you can explain exactly how.

 - Experience building strategy, not just running campaigns or managing partners. You've formed a thesis about where growth was hiding in a program, forecast it, executed it, and got other people to adopt it so it can compound and scale across a team.

 - Real comfort with data. You can analyze partner-level performance, build a forecast you'll defend, and tell the difference between a trend and noise, without waiting for someone to build you a report.

 - The ability to influence without authority. Much of your impact will come through people who don't report to you. Previous people-leadership experience is a real asset here.

 - Strong commercial instincts. You're confident pitching, handling objections, negotiating, and closing, and you keep a warm pipeline, warm.

 - Excellent judgment. You can assess brand fit and brand risk quickly, and you raise concerns early rather than after the fact.

 - Strong communication and project management skills. You'll coordinate directly with partners and across multiple internal teams to move work forward.

 - Ambition and humility. You don't accept the status quo simply because “it's what we've always done.” You push for better, newer, and more innovative ways to do things, all while staying humble.

 - Comfort wearing multiple hats. This is a hands-on role. Strategy sits alongside building a roster with campaign briefs, backend setup, contract tracking, and content monitoring.

 - The ability to travel. You may get the opportunity to represent Jobber during Ambassador brand trips, trade shows and other customer-related events across North America.

It would be really great (but not a deal-breaker) if you had:

 - Previous people-leadership experience.

 - Sales or business development experience at a SaaS company or tech startup.

 - Experience running paid campaigns on social media and with creators.

 - Experience with affiliate or partner management platforms and attribution tooling.

 - Education in Marketing, Business, Strategy, or related fields. BA, BS, MBA or MS in Marketing, Business or related field is a plus.

Location:

We believe great collaboration is intentional, and sometimes that means coming together in person to build, brainstorm, and connect. To support this, the role is open to candidates based in one of our hub cities: Edmonton, Toronto, Vancouver, or Kitchener-Waterloo.

Compensation:

At Jobber, we believe that compensation should be transparent, fair, and reflective of your experience and growth. This role has a minimum annual salary of $121,000, a midpoint of $142,200, and a maximum salary of $163,600, designed to show the progression from learning the ropes to truly excelling.

We design our compensation to reflect each new hire’s skills, experience against the complexity of the role, ensuring a fair and competitive salary. Our range is intentionally broad to support growth and long-term impact. For this role, we’re starting in the earlier portion of the range with room to grow further into the band as the role’s scope and impact expand. This approach ensures that compensation aligns with both the current shape of the role and the opportunity for growth as it evolves.

Base salary is just one part of a total compensation package that will include equity rewards, annual stipends for health and wellness, retirement savings matching, and an extended health package with fully paid premiums for body and mind. Your professional growth matters to us too! You’ll have access to a dedicated talent development program that includes career coaching and opportunities for career development.

We believe in transparency and open conversations about compensation. If you have any questions about our approach, we’re happy to discuss them throughout the hiring process!

What you can expect from Jobber:

 - A total compensation package that includes an extended health benefits package with fully paid premiums for both body and mind, matching in RRSP, TFSA or FHSA, and stock options.

 - A dedicated Talent Development team and access to coaching, learning, and leadership programs to help you grow your career, reach your goals, and unlock your full potential.

 - A unique opportunity to build, grow, and leave your impact on a $400-billion industry that has no dominant player...yet.

 - To work with a group of people who are humble, supportive, and give a sh*t about our customers.

We believe that diverse teams perform better and that fostering an inclusive work environment is a key part of growing a successful team. We welcome people of diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we are committed to working with applicants requesting accommodation at any stage of the hiring process.



A bit more about us:

Job by job, we’re transforming the way service is delivered. Your lawn care provider, home cleaning service, plumber or painter could use Jobber to better connect with their customers, save time in the office, invoice faster, and get paid! We’re bringing tens of thousands of people together with technology to deliver billions of dollars a year in services to happy customers. Jobber exists to help make these small businesses successful, and when they’re successful we all win!

 As the AVP, Triangle Digital, you will lead the strategy, development and delivery of digital experiences that support the Triangle loyalty program and create value for customers across Canadian Tire’s businesses. You will be accountable for shaping a clear digital vision, translating enterprise priorities into an actionable roadmap and ensuring that customer-facing experiences are simple, connected and engaging. Leading a team of digital product professionals, you will work closely with partners across Loyalty, Technology, Canadian Tire Bank, Lifecycle Marketing, Data and Analytics, and Store Operations to deliver measurable customer and business outcomes while building strong product management capabilities across the organization. 
 What you will do: 
 Lead, coach and develop the Triangle Digital team, establishing clear accountabilities and fostering a culture of collaboration, innovation, customer focus and consistent delivery. 
 Set the vision, strategy and multi-year roadmap for Triangle’s digital experiences and capabilities, aligned with broader loyalty and enterprise priorities. 
 Translate business priorities, customer needs and market opportunities into clear product plans, investment choices and measurable outcomes. 
 Oversee the design, delivery and ongoing improvement of customer-facing digital products and journeys across relevant channels and touchpoints. 
 Ensure digital experiences provide a consistent and compelling expression of the Triangle value proposition and support customer engagement, loyalty and growth. 
 Partner with Loyalty, Technology, Canadian Tire Bank, Lifecycle Marketing, Data and Analytics, Store Operations and other business teams to align priorities, clarify ownership, manage dependencies and deliver integrated experiences. 
 Build strong relationships with senior leaders and key partners, influencing decisions and creating alignment around the digital agenda. 
 Use customer insights, market trends, data and experimentation to guide priorities, improve experiences and strengthen business performance. 
 Establish clear performance measures and regularly assess progress, customer outcomes, operational health and the value delivered by the portfolio. 
 Lead annual and quarterly portfolio planning, prioritization, budgeting and resource allocation, balancing strategic investment with near-term business needs.

 Our software analyzes live network and media traffic in complex, mission-critical environments. It runs primarily on Linux across physical servers, virtual machines, containers, and cloud environments.
 Testing these systems involves more than clicking through a user interface. You may be validating an API response, checking database data, replaying network traffic, investigating a Linux service, or determining whether an unexpected result came from the application or the environment underneath it.
 You will help build and maintain automated regression suites and the infrastructure that supports them, including fixtures, test data, captured traffic, mocks, and simulated inputs.
 You do not need to come in knowing every part of our technology stack. We are looking for someone with a solid software and test automation foundation who is comfortable learning systems, networking, and deeper testing techniques as they grow in the role.

 Help maintain automated regression suites and investigate test failures
 Add and maintain smoke tests and automated checks in CI/CD pipelines
 Test REST APIs, including successful responses, failures, authentication, and edge cases
 Help build and maintain Linux, Docker, and virtual-machine based test environments
 Reproduce reported defects and add automated regression coverage where appropriate
 Investigate flaky tests and help identify their underlying causes
 Validate application behaviour against known inputs and expected outputs
 Test integrations such as APIs, syslog, SNMP, webhooks, and email notifications
 Assist with performance, load, and longer-running reliability tests
 Test installation, upgrade, and migration scenarios
 Debug failures across application, database, operating system, and network layers
 Work with developers to determine appropriate test coverage for new features
 Write clear defect reports with the information needed to reproduce and diagnose problems
 Participate in code reviews for test automation and tooling
 Contribute to testing AI-enabled features when required
 Tech Stack

 Python, Java, and TypeScript
 pytest, JUnit, Playwright, and Cypress
 REST APIs
 PostgreSQL and TimescaleDB
 Linux
 Docker and virtual machines
 CI/CD pipelines
 JIRA and Bitbucket
 Network and time-series data
 You do not need experience with every technology listed above.

 1-3 years of experience in software testing, test automation, software development, QA engineering, or a related technical role
 Programming or scripting experience, preferably with Python, Java, JavaScript, or TypeScript

 Experience testing REST APIs
 Basic experience with Git and modern software development workflows
 Comfortable working from the Linux command line

Owner is the AI-native system local business owners use to succeed, starting with restaurants.

We’re building the system that replaces the many tools owners use to run their business.

It powers everything from the restaurant’s website, online ordering, CRM, POS, and more.



Product philosophy

Most small business software makes owners do the work to get what they want: sales growth and profit growth. Owner does the work for them agentically.

Our system drives demand, converts it, and helps operators run their business day to day. As it improves, the business improves with it.

Using Owner should feel like having a team of great operators, engineers, and marketers working for you.



Our vision



We’re starting by helping independent restaurants succeed online.



But it’s not just restaurants that need our help. Most local businesses are struggling with these same problems. Huge technology corporations are taking their customers, bleeding their profits, and making it hard for them to survive.



Once we nail the solution for restaurants – we’ll scale it into every other local business type.



In the future we envision, tens of millions of local business owners will use our technology to succeed in the digital age.



Our traction



Since 2020, we've generated tens of millions in revenue and processed over a billion dollars of online orders. 1 in 5 Americans have used an Owner.com http://Owner.com website.

 What is the role
 We're looking for a Principal Software Developer to join the Elasticsearch - Search team. This globally-distributed team of expert engineers focuses on delivering a robust and feature-rich search experience, including contributing to improving the search experience in Lucene. This is a principal software engineering role that focuses on enhancing the vector similarity search functionality within Elasticsearch, covering the design and implementation of new vector search features, enhancements to existing vector search functionality, and resolving bugs.
 Our company is distributed by intention. We hire the best engineers we can find wherever they are, whoever they are. We collaborate across continents every day over email, GitHub, Zoom, and Slack.  Lead initiatives within Elasticsearch to produce an industry-leading vector database offering, supplying unparalleled speed and relevance in search.
 Contribute to Elasticsearch full time, building new search features and fixing intriguing bugs, all while making the code easier to understand. Sometimes you'll need to invent a new algorithm or data structure. Or find one and implement it. Sometimes you'll need to get close to the operating system and hardware.
 Work with a globally distributed team of experienced engineers focused on the vector search capabilities of Elasticsearch.
 Be an expert on how Elasticsearch implements vector similarity in support of search relevance and everyone will turn to you when they have a question about this area. You'll improve this area based on your questions and your instincts.
 Work with community members from all over the world on issues and pull requests, sometimes triaging them and handing them off to other experts and sometimes handling them yourself.
 Write idiomatic modern Java -- Elasticsearch is 99.8% Java!

 You have implemented novel techniques in vector similarity on a search platform with a large user base or progressed the field of academic research in vector similarity information retrieval.
 Professional experience with vector similarity and vector databases, and you used HNSW, IVF, or other relevant algorithms and libraries on search platforms at scale.

 You've used several data storage technologies like Elasticsearch, Solr, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, or Cassandra and have some idea how they work and why they work that way.
 You have excellent verbal and written communication skills. Like we said, collaborating on the internet is hard. We try to be respectful, empathetic, and trusting in all of our interactions. And we'd expect that from you too.

As we sharpen how every door in our retail fleet performs, this role will impact how we turn door-level performance into the allocation and replenishment decisions that put the right product, in the right depth, in the right store, at the right time.  You are an analytical self-starter who is equally at home in the data and in the room with Merchandising and Planning.  Door & fleet analysis (the core of the role)
 Own door-level performance analysis — sell-through, rate of sale, weeks of supply, in-stock rate, and productivity at the style, category, and price-point level.

 Allocation & replenishment
 Allocate and replenish product to doors against assortments, cluster minimums, capacity, and financial targets — balancing service level against excess and aged-inventory risk, and running rebalancing and inter-store transfers to chase demand.
 Own initial allocation for newness and new store openings — run the weekly product-drop cadence (allocation, store assortment updates, launch tracking), seed new launches with test-and-scale reads that inform go-forward depth, set opening buys for new doors as the fleet scales, and flag launch and delay risk early.

 Translate analysis into clear, headline-first recommendations for Merchandising, Planning, and Retail leadership, and run the weekly reporting rhythm that shows where the fleet is winning, where it's leaking, and what to do about it.

About Futurpreneur 
 Futurpreneur is a national non-profit organization that empowers diverse entrepreneurs, ages 18-39 to start, buy or grow their businesses in Canada, by providing loans with mentorship and resources. 
 Founded in 1996, we have helped more than 20,000 young entrepreneurs launch over 15,600 businesses, promoting entrepreneurship among Canadian youth as a critical pillar for strengthening the economy, generating employment opportunities, and fostering a sustainable future. 
 Futurpreneur is a founding member of the G20 Young Entrepreneurs’ Alliance , the Canadian founding member of Youth Business International and the Canadian host of Global Entrepreneurship Week (GEW) .  
 Our Purpose (why we exist): To drive inclusive Canadian prosperity by fostering the success of young entrepreneurs
 Our Mission (what we do every day to achieve our purpose): To empower diverse entrepreneurs ages 18-39 by providing loans with mentorship and resources to help them start and buy businesses that contribute to sustainable and inclusive economic prosperity, in their communities and across Canada.

 Convert entrepreneurial leads from inquiry through to application stage of our process

 Attend and coordinate events that provide opportunities to engage prospective and current entrepreneurs

 Create lead generation opportunities across region, while collaborating with existing and new partners

 Communicate with CRM regarding fulfilling mentor gaps.

 Follow-up with partners to make sure they have all the tools and information they need to represent us well with their customers. 
 Manage relationship with referral partners, as well as grow the number of partners if and where appropriate.
 Participate as required in the activities of partners in the ecosystem to engage community partners and recruit entrepreneurs in search of financing and mentorship.

 Identify potential partners through research, events, networks and referrals

 Must have a valid driver’s license and access to a vehicle (40% of this role includes local and provincial travel).  
 Relevant experience may include education with a focus on business administration, economic development, entrepreneurship or equivalent hands-on career experience.  
 3+ years of experience in sales, start-up business development or economic development position. 
 Bilingualism in French & English (spoken & written) is an asset.
 Experience working with entrepreneurs or business startups, business plans and cashflows is considered a strong asset. 
 Ability to tailor and deliver public program presentations and workshops.

 Strong client focus with the ability to work with volunteers.  
 Confident, proactive and motivated, able to work with a minimum of supervision. 
 Strong ability to work both independently and as part of a team.  
 Knowledge of trends within the entrepreneurial, startup, small business industry.

 Clear and confident communicator, skilled at engaging and connecting with diverse audiences.

 Strong organizational skills, able to balance multiple priorities effectively in a dynamic hybrid work environment.
 Demonstrate curiosity and a growth mindset, embracing and championing change.

Build the demand engine for Acuity’s next stage of growth. 
 Acuity Insights is entering a new stage of growth. We’ve spent years building products used by higher education programs to make important decisions about who enters their programs and how learners are supported once they get there. Today, established products are evolving, newer products are being commercialized, and we’re exploring how to reach new audiences and markets.
 As our Senior Growth Marketing Manager , you’ll help turn that opportunity into demand.
 You’re not walking into a blank slate, and you’re not inheriting a finished playbook. You’ll have enough foundation to move quickly and enough room to bring your own experience, ideas, and point of view to what comes next.
 You’ll have working campaigns, a strong webinar program, recurring prospect communications, established cross-functional partners, and improving data and measurement capabilities to build from.
 You’ll also have real whitespace. Nurture is a capability we need to build. International demand generation is largely unexplored. And we want you to bring the AI practices you’re already using in Growth Marketing to help accelerate our adoption, from campaign development and content repurposing to research, testing, and analysis. Across all of it, we want to get much better at understanding what creates qualified pipeline and contributes to revenue.
 You’ll be our only dedicated Growth Marketer, working hands-on across strategy and execution while surrounded by partners across Marketing and our broader Growth organization. This opportunity will suit you particularly well if you like getting close to the business, figuring out where marketing can have the greatest commercial impact, and turning that judgment into action.
 Before you apply: This is full-time, 16-month fixed-term employment covering an upcoming parental leave, open to candidates based anywhere in Canada. The start date is early November 2026. You’ll work remotely within Canada with access to employee benefits including healthcare coverage, paid time off, and a learning and development budget. 
 Thoughtful use of AI is welcome. If you use it to support your application, please make sure it helps communicate your experience clearly and accurately. Authenticity and originality will help you stand out. 
 The Work You’ll Do
 You’ll start with Acuity’s company-wide onboarding program, building context on our business, products, customers, and how we work. From there, you’ll go deeper into Marketing and our broader Growth organization, getting close to the campaigns, data, priorities, relationships, and rhythms that shape Growth Marketing today.
 As you ramp, you’ll take increasing ownership of demand generation across our product portfolio, with the context and relationships you need to make good decisions and move independently.
 Take ownership of demand generation 
 You’ll set and run our quarterly demand-generation plans, deciding how Growth Marketing can best contribute to our commercial priorities and where to focus across competing opportunities.
 That means moving comfortably between strategy and execution: identifying the audiences and opportunities worth pursuing, choosing the right channels and tactics, building and launching the work, measuring what happens, and using what you learn to decide what comes next.
 You’ll have autonomy to bring your own judgment and experience to the work, while staying closely connected to the business priorities, product developments, and customer insights that should shape it.
 Turn product momentum into demand 
 You’ll work across a portfolio at different stages of maturity. Casper and One45 are established products with deep roots in higher education, with One45 now evolving into its next chapter. Video Interviews and Professional Skills Development are newer solutions we’re actively commercializing.
 Working with Product Marketing, Sales, Customer Success and Business Development, you’ll translate product positioning, market insight, customer needs, and commercialization priorities into demand-generation strategies that reach the right audiences and give them a reason to engage.
 You’ll gather context, develop a point of view about how Growth Marketing can contribute, recommend an approach, and carry it into market.
 Build demand across the funnel 
 You’ll architect, execute, and optimize integrated campaigns across the channels that make sense for the audience and opportunity, including paid media, email, web, content, prospect communications, and new approaches worth testing.
 You’ll continue building on a webinar program that has shown strong potential for generating qualified demand, owning the Growth Marketing motion end-to-end from audience and promotion strategy through registration, follow-up, and measurement.
 And you’ll build and evolve nurture programs beyond their current state: developing more intentional journeys for different audiences and verticals, identifying useful triggers and segmentation, and creating paths that help accelerate leads toward sales readiness.
 Get closer to what actually drives growth 
 You’ll help us become much more disciplined about asking: What worked? What generated qualified demand? What progressed into pipeline? What contributed to revenue? And what should we do differently next time?
 Using HubSpot, campaign data, and our evolving business intelligence capabilities, you’ll look beyond surface-level engagement metrics to understand how Growth Marketing contributes further down the funnel.
 You’ll establish stronger measurement rhythms, test targeting and messaging, compare performance across campaigns and channels, and use what you learn to make better decisions about where we invest our time and budget.
 You won’t control every downstream revenue outcome, but you’ll understand the connection between your work and the commercial funnel and take accountability for continuously improving that contribution.
 Put AI to work in Growth Marketing 
 You’ll bring AI practices that are already part of your toolkit and help us apply them meaningfully at Acuity. That could include campaign development, research, content creation and repurposing, nurture, experimentation, and analysis, as well as use cases we haven’t identified yet.
 The goal isn’t AI for its own sake. It’s finding practical ways to reduce manual work, get more leverage from what we create, improve quality and speed, and make better decisions. When something works, you’ll help turn it into a practice the broader team can learn from and continue using.
 Test how we generate demand internationally 
 As Acuity expands its international reach, you’ll help us learn how our demand-generation approach translates into priority market including Australia and New Zealand (ANZ), UK and Ireland.
 Working with partners across Growth, you’ll develop and run a focused demand-generation pilot in one of these markets. You’ll help determine the audience, messaging, channels, and measures of success, then use what happens in this market to build an evidence-based point of view about what we should test, change, or invest in next.
 Who You’ll Work With, and How
 You’ll report to our Director of Marketing and join a Marketing function that includes Marketing Operations, Digital Marketing, Customer Marketing, Events Marketing, Content and Communications.
 You’ll be our dedicated Growth Marketing expert. That means bringing your own expertise while knowing how to draw on the expertise around you.
 Sales and Business Development will be particularly important partners. They’re close to prospective customers every day and can help you understand the problems buyers are talking about, the language they use, what resonates, where opportunities are stalling, and what they’re hearing in the higher education market.
 You’ll collaborate with Customer Success to dig deeper into buyer insights, source speakers for virtual events, understand expansion opportunities, and amplify post-event follow-up.
 Your job is to listen closely, connect those insights with what you know about demand generation, and turn them into a point of view and a plan. Collaboration here doesn’t mean waiting for consensus or for someone else to tell you what campaign to run.
 You’ll work closely with Product Marketing to understand positioning, value propositions, audiences, and product messaging, then translate that foundation into campaigns and experiences designed for the people we want to reach.
 Within Marketing, you’ll collaborate with Customer Marketing, Events Marketing, Communications, Marketing Operations, and Creative teams to bring campaigns, customer proof points, thought leadership, webinars, and other experiences to life. 
 And with RevOps, you’ll strengthen the connection between marketing activity, lead progression, pipeline, and revenue so what we learn can shape what we do next.
 You won’t need to know everything yourself. You will need to know your craft, build strong relationships, ask good questions, make recommendations, and keep things moving.
 The Impact You’ll Have
 Over the course of your time with us, you’ll help build a stronger and more scalable demand-generation engine. Your impact will show up in:
 Greater commercial accountability. We’ll have clearer visibility into which campaigns, channels, audiences, and messages are creating qualified demand, progressing into pipeline, and contributing to revenue.
 A stronger nurture capability. We’ll have more intentional journeys for different audiences and verticals, giving promising demand more opportunities to progress toward sales readiness.
 Stronger commercialization. Professional Skills Development, Video Interviews, and the continued evolution of One45 will have focused demand-generation strategies supporting their growth in market.
 A more connected event-to-demand engine. Webinars and virtual events will connect more intentionally to follow-up, nurture, pipeline progression, and what we learn from each program.
 AI practices that create real leverage. We’ll have practical, proven ways of using AI to improve how Growth Marketing researches, creates, experiments, analyzes, and gets more from the work we produce.
 Evidence to inform international growth. We’ll have real market learnings from demand-generation experimentation in a priority international market, giving us a stronger foundation for what to test or invest in next.
 Across all of it, you’ll help us make growth decisions with more evidence and confidence, while leaving the demand engine stronger than you found it.
 How You’ll Succeed Here
 There’s no single profile for success in this role. But the person who thrives here will probably recognize themselves in a few things.
 You think commercially. 
Campaign activity is interesting to you because of what happens next. You want to understand whether people engaged, whether they became qualified opportunities, whether pipeline moved, and what that tells you about where to invest next.
 You bring a point of view. 
You listen to Sales, Business Development, Product, customer insights, market data,, but you don’t need everyone else to design the answer for you. You synthesize what you’ve learned, make recommendations, and move the work forward proactively.
 You know how to create momentum with what you have. 
You don’t need a huge budget, a large team, or a perfectly established playbook before you can make progress. You’re resourceful about figuring out what matters most, where to focus, and what you can build, test, or improve with the resources around you.
 You’re genuinely hands-on. 
You move fluidly between planning and doing, comfortably zooming out to set campaign strategy or diving into an ad platform, webinar plan, landing page, or email flow to make it real. You don't need a large team around you to move work forward. You can inherit something that already works, respect what has been built, and still see where it could become better.
 You experiment with purpose. 
You’re willing to try something new, but experimentation isn’t throwing ideas at a wall. You start with a hypothesis, look at what happened, learn from it, and decide whether to iterate, scale, or stop.
 You use AI as part of your craft. 
You’ve moved beyond simply being curious about AI. You’re already using it in your work, learning where it creates leverage, where human judgment matters, and how it can help you move faster or produce better work.
 You’re comfortable making choices. 
You've worked in environments where priorities evolve and the playbook isn't always complete. You bring structure, judgment, and a bias toward action while staying focused on measurable business impact. 
 Experience That Will Help You Hit the Ground Running
 We care more about what you’ve actually owned, built, learned, and improved.
 You’ll likely bring experience: 
 Owning B2B demand generation with accountability for qualified leads, pipeline, and commercial outcomes, ideally in SaaS or another complex B2B environment.
 Personally designing, launching, measuring, and optimizing integrated campaigns across channels such as paid media, email, web, content, nurture, and virtual events.
 Bringing a new product or meaningful product development to market and building demand around it.
 Independently planning and executing webinars or other virtual events end to end, including content strategy, speaker sourcing, promotion, event flow, live execution, and post-event follow-up.
 Using marketing and funnel data to evaluate performance, identify patterns, make investment decisions, and understand how marketing activity contributes to pipeline and revenue.
 Building or significantly improving nurture programs, segmentation, automation flows, and recurring prospect communications using HubSpot or similar platforms.
 Partnering closely with Sales and Product Marketing to turn customer, market, and product insight into effective demand-generation strategies.
 Using AI meaningfully in your day-to-day marketing work to improve the quality, speed, analysis, or scale of what you produce.
 Experience generating demand outside North America, particularly in Australia/New Zealand or the UK/Ireland, would be valuable as we begin testing our approach in these markets.
 And if you’ve previously been the only Growth Marketer, or one of very few, you’ll bring particularly relevant experience for the level of ownership this role offers.
 How We Support You
 Transparent compensation. A salary between $110,000–$135,000 CAD, aligned to role scope, experience, and internal equity.
 Learning that grows with you. A $3,000 annual learning budget to invest in your development, to deepen your expertise, build new skills, or explore new areas of interest.
 Remote-first work. Fully remote within Canada, with up to six weeks per year to work internationally.
 Time to rest and reset. Self-directed vacation (most teammates take 4–6 weeks annually), monthly Acuity Days (a collective Friday off), plus a two-week company-wide closure each December.
 Comprehensive care. Health benefits from day one for you and your dependents.
 What Happens After You Apply
 We review every application carefully and don’t use AI to evaluate candidates, though you may be automatically screened out if you don’t meet baseline requirements such as Canadian residency and valid work authorization. AI may support note-taking in some interviews, but people make every evaluation and hiring decision.
 Our interviews are two-way conversations: a chance for us to understand your experience and what you’re looking for, and for you to get to know Acuity, the role, and the people you’d work with. The process typically takes 2–4 weeks from first conversation to final decision.
 Steps in the Process
 Application Review. A member of our Talent team reviews your application.
 Intro Conversation. You’ll meet with a member of our Talent team to explore your experience, what you’re looking for next, and learn more broadly about Acuity Insights and the opportunity. 
 Conversation with the Manager. You’ll meet our Director of Marketing to dig into the growth work you’ve owned, the decisions you’ve made, and the results. If you have something you can share, we’ll invite you to bring an example of real work you’re proud of so we can explore how you approached it and what you learned.
 Team Conversations. You’ll meet a few of the people you’d work with closely to explore how you collaborate, solve problems, and move work forward, while getting a better feel for what working together would be like.
 Decision. We bring together feedback from your conversations and typically make a decision within 2–4 business days.
 Offer & Reference Checks. If it’s a match, we’ll move to references and a formal offer.
 Life at Acuity Insights
 We’re a remote-first team of 135+ people, built around trust, flexibility, and giving people meaningful ownership of their work.
 Remote-first doesn’t mean working in isolation. We collaborate closely across teams, communicate thoughtfully across time zones, and create intentional opportunities to connect, while protecting the flexibility and focus that make remote work valuable.
 Day to day, you can expect:
 High trust and autonomy in how you get your work done
 Thoughtful, async-friendly communication across a distributed team
 Space for focused work alongside intentional collaboration and connection
 Colleagues who are generous with their expertise and expect you to bring yours
 A sustainable approach to work that values impact over performative busyness
 As we grow, we’re deliberate about evolving how we work without adding process for process’s sake. We want people to have the clarity, context, relationships, and room to make good decisions and do work they’re proud of.
 About Acuity Insights
 Acuity Insights builds products that help higher education institutions make better decisions about people, from admissions through to development.
 Our work is grounded in a simple idea: that people are more than their grades, and that potential can be understood and developed, not just measured.
 Our Casper situational judgment test (SJT), created by researchers at McMaster University, has been completed by over 1 million applicants and is one of the most widely used open-response SJTs in higher education, backed by nearly 20 years of research.
 Today, we are evolving our products to better connect assessment, insight, and development, helping institutions not just identify potential, but actively support its growth over time. As part of that evolution, we’re increasingly building toward a more connected ecosystem across assessment, education, and learner development. While teams remain focused on their individual products, we’re creating stronger connections across our platform to deliver more cohesive experiences for institutions and learners.
